headline: Make your site [load fast]
sub: Speed is the first feature users notice.
points: Cache static files with a CDN
cta: Save this for your next build
caption:
⚡ A slow site loses visitors before they read a word. Quick wins: modern image formats, lazy loading, less JavaScript and a CDN for static files.

headline: Ship it, then [improve] it.
sub: A working v1 beats a perfect idea that never launches.
caption:
🚀 Your first version will not be perfect, and that is fine. Launch small, get real feedback, then improve. Users can't use the app that lives only in your head.

headline: Build your first [mobile app]
points: Pick one: Flutter or React Native
Build one screen that solves one problem
Add a backend like Supabase or Firebase
Test on a real phone, then publish
caption:
📱 Want to build your first app? Choose one cross-platform framework, solve one small problem on one screen, connect a ready backend and test on a real device before publishing.

headline: Center anything with [Flexbox]
sub: Three lines. Every time.
caption:
🎯 Still fighting to center a div? Put these three lines on the parent: display flex, justify-content center, align-items center. Done. Grid works too: display grid + place-items center.

headline: Never commit your [secrets]
sub: One leaked key can cost you everything.
caption:
🔐 API keys pushed to GitHub get found by bots within minutes. Keep secrets in environment variables, ignore your .env file and rotate any key that was ever exposed.

headline: Your GitHub is your [CV].
sub: Build real projects and show them.
caption:
💼 Employers and clients want proof, not just certificates. A few finished, well-documented projects on GitHub say more than a long list of skills.

headline: Make it [responsive] from day one
sub: Most of your users are on a phone.
points: Use rem, %, and clamp() for sizes
cta: Open your site on a phone
caption:
📲 Most visitors will open your site on a phone. Design mobile-first, use flexible units, test small screens early and keep buttons big enough to tap.

headline: A clean [Git] workflow
points: Create a branch for each feature
Open a pull request and review
Merge to main and delete the branch
cta: Try it on your next feature
caption:
🌿 A simple Git habit saves teams hours: one branch per feature, small commits with clear messages, a pull request for review, then merge and clean up.

headline: Design APIs people [love] to use
sub: Good APIs feel obvious.
caption:
🔌 A good API needs almost no explanation. Clear resource names, correct HTTP status codes, pagination for big lists and real examples in the docs.

headline: Build projects, not [tutorials].
sub: Tutorials teach syntax. Projects teach you to think.
caption:
🧠 Stuck in tutorial hell? Close the video and build something you actually need: a to-do app, a budget tracker, a portfolio. You learn most when you get stuck and fix it yourself.

headline: Make your app feel [fast]
sub: Perceived speed matters as much as real speed.
caption:
⚡ Users judge an app's speed in the first second. Skeleton screens, offline caching, progressive images and instant tap feedback make any app feel faster.

headline: Debug like a [pro]
sub: Stop guessing. Start narrowing.
cta: Use this on your next bug
caption:
🐞 Most bugs are found by narrowing, not guessing. Reproduce it, read the whole error, look at what changed recently and test small pieces until only the problem is left.

headline: Write code for the [next] developer.
sub: That developer is usually you, six months later.
caption:
✍️ Clear names, small functions and a short comment where the 'why' isn't obvious. Future-you will be grateful.

Deploy free on Vercel or Netlify
Connect the domain and add HTTPS
caption:
🌍 Getting online is easier than ever: grab a domain, build from a template or framework, deploy free on Vercel or Netlify and connect your domain with free HTTPS.

headline: Keep your database [fast]
sub: Small habits, big speed.
points: Fetch only the fields you need
caption:
🗄️ A slow app is often a slow database. Add indexes on columns you filter by, select only what you need, avoid N+1 queries and paginate large results.

headline: Build for [everyone]
sub: Accessible sites are better sites.
points: Make it work with a keyboard
caption:
♿ Accessibility helps every user, not just some. Alt text, strong contrast, labelled inputs and full keyboard support are simple to add from the start.

headline: Sell [solutions], not code.
sub: Clients pay for results.
caption:
💡 Clients don't buy 'a React website'. They buy more customers, less paperwork, faster orders. Talk about the problem you solve, and the price conversation gets easier.

headline: Before you [publish] your app
sub: A quick launch checklist.
points: Test on old and new phones
caption:
✅ Before you hit publish on Play Store or App Store: test on different devices, add a privacy policy, prepare great screenshots and turn on crash reporting.

headline: Write [cleaner] JavaScript
sub: Modern syntax that reads better.
caption:
🟨 Small modern JavaScript habits make code easier to read: const by default, optional chaining, nullish coalescing and async/await.

points: Write the one problem it solves
Put it in front of 10 real users
caption:
🛠️ An MVP is the smallest thing that proves your idea. One problem, only must-have features, a short build, then real users and feedback.

sub: Basics every app needs.
points: Validate all input on the server
caption:
🛡️ Security basics that every web and mobile app needs: hashed passwords, server-side validation, HTTPS everywhere and rate-limited logins.

sub: Minutes saved every hour add up to days.
caption:
⌨️ Multi-cursor, go to file, rename symbol, format document. Learn a few editor shortcuts each week and you'll code noticeably faster.

sub: Simple rules, big difference.
points: Stick to a small color palette
caption:
🎨 You don't need to be a designer for a clean UI: limit fonts and colors, add more white space and use consistent spacing everywhere.

caption:

caption:

caption:

caption:

caption:
